## Purpose and Entry Points
Crawl4AI is a Python 3.10+ asynchronous web-crawling and scraping SDK that turns web pages into LLM-ready Markdown and optional structured data. Primary SDK entry point is `AsyncWebCrawler`; package exports originate in `crawl4ai/__init__.py`. User-facing execution paths include the CLI in `crawl4ai/cli.py`, install/setup commands in `crawl4ai/install.py`, and an optional Docker REST service in `deploy/docker/server.py`.

## Core Crawl Orchestration
`AsyncWebCrawler` owns crawler lifecycle and exposes single-URL (`arun`) and batch/streaming workflows. It composes browser strategy, run configuration, caching, scraping, Markdown generation, extraction, and result models. Runtime configuration and public contracts are concentrated in `crawl4ai/async_configs.py`, `crawl4ai/models.py`, and `crawl4ai/types.py`. This is the central boundary between SDK callers and crawl implementation.

## Browser and Network Acquisition
Browser-backed crawling is mediated by strategy and lifecycle layers: `crawl4ai/async_crawler_strategy.py`, `crawl4ai/browser_manager.py`, and `crawl4ai/browser_adapter.py`. The default runtime is Playwright, including local/persistent contexts and CDP-connected browsers. Browser configuration governs JavaScript execution, sessions, screenshots/PDFs, resource filtering, profiles, user agents, proxies, and stealth-oriented behavior. HTTP/direct-fetch alternatives remain behind crawler strategies rather than changing the caller API.

## Content Processing Pipeline
After acquisition, HTML is scraped into page content, links, media, and metadata, then transformed into Markdown and optional fitted/relevant content. Key stage boundaries are `crawl4ai/content_scraping_strategy.py`, `crawl4ai/markdown_generation_strategy.py`, and `crawl4ai/content_filter_strategy.py`. HTML-to-text conversion is internally packaged in `crawl4ai/html2text/`. Results may also include tables via `crawl4ai/table_extraction.py` and parsed PDFs via `crawl4ai/processors/pdf/processor.py`.

## Extraction and AI Integration
Extraction is strategy-driven: CSS/XPath/schema extraction and LLM-based structured extraction are implemented from `crawl4ai/extraction_strategy.py`, with chunking in `crawl4ai/chunking_strategy.py`. LLM configuration, prompts, and provider access are separated through `crawl4ai/async_configs.py`, `crawl4ai/prompts.py`, and `crawl4ai/model_loader.py`; providers are externally supplied through LiteLLM-compatible configuration. This keeps crawling usable without API keys while allowing model-backed extraction, filtering, adaptive crawling, and table extraction.

## Multi-URL Discovery and Traversal
Concurrency and scheduling for bulk work are handled by `crawl4ai/async_dispatcher.py`. Deep crawling is a separate traversal subsystem with shared strategy interfaces plus BFS, DFS, and best-first implementations in `crawl4ai/deep_crawling/base_strategy.py`, `crawl4ai/deep_crawling/bfs_strategy.py`, and `crawl4ai/deep_crawling/bff_strategy.py`. It applies filters/scorers, supports cancellation and resumable state, and delegates each discovered URL back into the normal crawl pipeline. URL discovery/seeding is separately provided by `crawl4ai/async_url_seeder.py`.

## Persistence, Safety, and Deployment
Caching and crawl persistence are isolated in `crawl4ai/cache_context.py`, `crawl4ai/cache_validator.py`, and `crawl4ai/async_database.py`. Anti-bot detection and retry/proxy escalation sit at the fetch boundary in `crawl4ai/antibot_detector.py` and `crawl4ai/proxy_strategy.py`. Docker deployment exposes a FastAPI-based job API, browser pool, monitoring, Redis-backed coordination/configuration, webhooks, and MCP bridge through `deploy/docker/api.py`, `deploy/docker/crawler_pool.py`, and `deploy/docker/work_queue.py`. Its security boundary treats requests as untrusted: auth, egress controls, hook execution, artifact handling, and SSRF defenses are distinct modules under `deploy/docker/`.
